summary: This lecture opens the year of sorrow in the Prophet's life. After the boycott ended, because the pact was eaten by termites and through the effort of five men, Abu Talib fell ill after protecting the Prophet SAW for about 42 years. The Prophet SAW pleaded with him to say La ilaha illallah, but Abu Jahal and Abu Sufyan goaded him not to abandon his forefathers' religion, and he died without saying it. Allah revealed that the Prophet SAW cannot give guidance to those he loves. Khadijah RA, ill from the boycott, then died after Jibril conveyed Allah's greeting and news of a pearl palace in paradise. The Prophet SAW and the young Fatimah and Umm Kulthum grieved deeply, and he always remembered Khadijah. The ustaz urges kindness to orphans.
keyPoints: The year of sorrow is the year the Prophet SAW lost Abu Talib and Khadijah RA.
The Prophet SAW pleaded with Abu Talib to say La ilaha illallah, but Abu Jahal and Abu Sufyan goaded him until he died without saying it.
Allah explained that the Prophet SAW cannot give guidance to those he loves.
Jibril conveyed Allah's greeting to Khadijah and news of a pearl palace in paradise.
The Prophet SAW said Allah never replaced Khadijah with someone better, and always remembered her.

chapters.title: Opening: the year of sorrow
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens with Abu Talib's last moments and introduces the year of sorrow, when the Prophet SAW was not seen smiling.

chapters.title: Hardship in the camp and Gaza
chapters.summary: A companion ate dried animal hide, and the ustaz compares this with an Egyptian man killed for trying to cheer Gaza's children.

chapters.title: The boycott ends and a new trial
chapters.summary: The ustaz recaps the two factors that ended the boycott, and the deepest trial that followed, losing Abu Talib.

chapters.title: Abu Talib on his deathbed
chapters.summary: Abu Talib, who cared for the Prophet SAW since he was eight, was dying, and the Prophet SAW tried to save his hereafter.

chapters.title: The Prophet's plea and Quraysh's goading
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW asked for one phrase, but Abu Jahal and Abu Sufyan taunted Abu Talib not to leave his ancestors' religion.

chapters.title: Abu Talib's real name
chapters.summary: The ustaz explains his real name was Abdul Manaf ibn Abdul Muttalib and that Mecca's notables came to visit him.

chapters.title: Abu Talib dies and Ali
chapters.summary: Abu Talib died without saying it and the Prophet SAW was deeply sad. Ali told his father, and the Prophet SAW had him handle the burial.

chapters.title: Khadijah as comforter
chapters.summary: Khadijah embraced and encouraged the Prophet SAW each day, yet she herself was gravely ill from the boycott.

chapters.title: Allah's greeting and the pearl palace
chapters.summary: Jibril conveyed the greetings of Allah and himself to Khadijah along with a pearl palace free of fatigue and noise.

chapters.title: The verse on guidance
chapters.summary: Allah revealed that the Prophet SAW cannot guide those he loves, and the ustaz stresses there is no compulsion in Islam.

chapters.title: The Prophet's daughters and orphans
chapters.summary: The ustaz lists the Prophet's daughters, estimates Fatimah's age, and encourages kindness to orphans.

chapters.title: Khadijah dies
chapters.summary: Khadijah died before the five prayers were prescribed; the Prophet SAW shrouded her himself and she was buried at al-Ma'alla.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW remembers Khadijah
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW wept at home, gave gifts to Khadijah's friends, and stressed Allah never replaced her with someone better.

chapters.title: Closing: visiting graves and next class
chapters.summary: The ustaz prays to visit Mecca and Madinah, and says the Prophet SAW would leave to seek a new place.

dalil.context: The ustaz recites part of the verse that the Prophet SAW cannot guide those he loves.
dalil.translation: You [Prophet] cannot guide everyone you love to the truth; it is God who guides whoever He will: He knows best those who will follow guidance.
The Prophet SAW said: O my uncle, say one phrase, La ilaha illallah, and I will plead for you before Allah.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates the Prophet's plea at Abu Talib's final moment. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: Jibril told the Prophet SAW that Khadijah was coming with food, and he was to convey greetings from her Lord and from Jibril, with news of a house in paradise of pearl free of noise and fatigue.
dalil.context: The ustaz says some scholars place this a few days before Khadijah died. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said that whoever is kind to and cares for an orphan will be in paradise with him, side by side.
dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this while urging students to be kind to orphans. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: When Aisha said Allah had replaced Khadijah with someone better, the Prophet SAW replied that He had not: she believed when others rejected and gave her wealth when others withheld.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates Aisha's remark and the Prophet's reply. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.role: The uncle who raised the Prophet SAW
people.context: Raised the Prophet SAW from age eight, provided the land for the boycott camp, but died without the shahada.
Present at Abu Talib's bedside and taunted him not to leave his ancestors' religion.
Also present and goaded Abu Talib.
Embraced Islam at seven, told his father, and buried him at the Prophet's order.
Comforted the Prophet SAW daily, fell ill from the boycott, and died before the five prayers were prescribed.
Conveyed Allah's greeting to Khadijah with news of the pearl palace.
Still young, about nine or ten, when her mother died.
Lived at home with Fatimah, about two years older.
Asked why the Prophet SAW always spoke of Khadijah.

sirah.era: The year of sorrow: the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the end of the boycott, the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah RA, and the Prophet's grief.

events.label: Boycott ends
events.title: The boycott is ended
events.desc: The pact was eaten by termites and five men moved against it.

events.label: Abu Talib
events.title: Abu Talib falls ill and is pleaded with
events.desc: The Prophet SAW held his hand and asked him to say La ilaha illallah.

events.label: Death
events.title: Abu Talib dies
events.desc: He did not say the shahada and Ali saw to his burial.

events.label: Greeting
events.title: Allah's greeting to Khadijah
events.desc: Jibril conveyed the greeting and news of a pearl palace.

events.label: Verse
events.title: The verse on guidance
events.desc: Allah affirmed that guidance is His alone.

events.label: Khadijah dies
events.title: Khadijah RA dies
events.desc: The Prophet SAW shrouded and buried her at al-Ma'alla.

events.label: Memory
events.title: The Prophet SAW remembers Khadijah
events.desc: He wept at night and gave gifts to her friends.

lessons.title: Guidance belongs to Allah
lessons.body: Even the Prophet SAW could not force those he loved to embrace Islam; our task is to convey.

lessons.title: Understanding converts' struggles
lessons.body: New Muslims struggle because loved family are not yet Muslim, so speak with compassion.

lessons.title: The danger of pride and goading
lessons.body: Abu Talib did not say it out of pride in his father and being taunted as a traitor.

lessons.title: Loving orphans
lessons.body: Those who care for orphans will be near the Prophet SAW in paradise, and he himself was an orphan.

lessons.title: A spouse who comforts
lessons.body: Khadijah was where the Prophet SAW returned to be comforted after being insulted.

lessons.title: Remembering those who served us
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW gave gifts to Khadijah's friends and always praised her.

lessons.title: Gratitude for our ease
lessons.body: We were born into Muslim families, so do not speak lightly to those who have not.

lessons.title: Feelings change
lessons.body: Ordinary sadness comes and goes, but the year of sorrow lasted all year.

lessons.title: The five prayers were not yet prescribed
lessons.body: At that time there were only two prayers and no funeral prayer, so the Prophet SAW shrouded Khadijah himself.
